Against that, ordinary life carries on — a world title could be decided on track tonight, and Apple's new leadership faces its first real test tomorrow, two days before America votes.

sections.title: World
sections.gist: A near-70 death Spanish rail crash, Israel's fraught coalition talks and Tuesday's US midterms dominated world news today.

items.headline: Toledo train crash toll near 70, ex-minister among dead
items.what: A Renfe train rear-ended a stopped Iryo train near Toledo on October 28. The death toll has climbed to at least 68, including former Spanish employment minister Fátima Báñez. More than 100 people were injured, with 58 hospitalised and 15 in serious condition.
items.why_it_matters: It raises hard questions about rail safety on one of Spain's busiest lines, just as the transport minister calls the stop order 'inexplicable.'
items.context: Spain runs high-speed trains on shared tracks operated by state-run Renfe and private rival Iryo. This is the country's second deadly derailment this year, after a January crash killed 45 people.
items.next: Investigators are focused on the signal fault behind the halt order; PM Sánchez has promised accountability.
items.insight: Two serious crashes on Spain's rail network in ten months point to a system-wide signalling problem, not a one-off error.

items.headline: Israel's Herzog begins talks on who forms government
items.what: President Isaac Herzog is consulting party leaders after the October 27 election left no bloc with the 61 seats needed to govern. Likud ally Benny Biton says Netanyahu now wants a unity government with rival Gadi Eisenkot. Likud has also claimed, without evidence, that the vote was rigged.
items.why_it_matters: Weeks of coalition haggling, or a repeat election, could leave Israel without a working government during a fragile Gaza truce.
items.context: Herzog is Israel's ceremonial president, who picks who gets first shot at building a coalition. Netanyahu's bloc and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc are both short of the 61-seat majority, after weeks of disputed vote counts.
items.next: Herzog's consultations continue this week; official results, which could still shift, are due November 4.
items.insight: An unfounded fraud claim after a narrow loss is a familiar play — the real fight is which small parties defect to break the deadlock.

items.headline: America votes Tuesday in high-stakes midterm elections
items.what: Americans vote this Tuesday, November 3, in midterm elections that decide control of Congress. Trump has pledged over $400 million to help Republicans, and more than 18 million people have already voted early. Polls are tight, and a fake polling firm's fabricated numbers have muddied forecasts further.
items.why_it_matters: The outcome shapes everything from tariffs to immigration policy for the next two years.
items.context: Midterms fall halfway through a president's term, when the whole House and a third of the Senate are up for election. The result decides if Trump keeps a friendly Congress for his last two years, or faces gridlock.
items.next: Polls close Tuesday night; control of the House and Senate should be known within hours.

sections.title: Affects you
sections.gist: Delhi's ban on outside dirty trucks began today as the capital's air stayed hazardous.

items.headline: Delhi's ban on outside dirty trucks takes effect today
items.what: Delhi's border ban on non-BS-VI commercial vehicles registered outside the city started today, November 1, as planned. Only electric, CNG and BS-VI diesel buses may now enter; others are turned back at the border. Delhi's air stayed severe to hazardous today, with real-time monitors reporting AQI readings between 267 and 322.
items.why_it_matters: If you're outside today in Delhi, air this bad raises real risks for breathing, the heart, and young children.
items.context: The ban is part of Delhi's winter pollution plan, when cold, still air traps vehicle and construction smoke over the city. AQI, the Air Quality Index, measures how polluted the air is — above 300 is 'hazardous' to breathe.
items.next: Authorities can add stricter curbs — on construction, generators or older cars — if pollution worsens further.
items.insight: Conflicting sensor readings (267 vs 322) show why one single 'AQI number' for Delhi is misleading — always check your own locality.

terms.meaning: Bharat Stage VI — India's strictest vehicle emissions standard, used since 2020.
Air Quality Index — a 0-500+ scale; above 300 is considered hazardous.

sections.title: Markets & money
sections.gist: Apple's Q4 earnings tomorrow will be new CEO John Ternus's first big test with investors.

items.headline: Apple reports Q4 earnings tomorrow, its first under new CEO
items.what: Apple reports fiscal Q4 2026 earnings after the market closes on Monday, November 2. It's the first earnings call led by new CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on September 1. Apple's own guidance points to revenue of roughly $112-114 billion for the quarter, up about 9-11% from last year.
items.why_it_matters: It's the clearest early signal yet of whether Apple's new leadership can keep iPhone sales and AI plans on track.
items.context: Apple's fiscal year runs a quarter ahead of the calendar, so this report covers June to September sales, the new iPhone's launch quarter. Ternus, a 25-year Apple veteran who led iPhone and Mac engineering, replaced Cook as CEO after a long-planned handover.
items.next: Results land after US markets close Monday; a call with analysts follows at 2pm Pacific time.
items.insight: A smooth first earnings call matters more for investor confidence in Ternus than the numbers themselves — markets are really grading the handover.

sections.title: Formula 1
sections.gist: Hamilton took a stunning Ferrari pole, but all eyes are on whether Antonelli clinches the F1 title tonight.

items.headline: Hamilton grabs first Ferrari pole as Antonelli eyes F1 title
items.what: Lewis Hamilton out-qualified Mercedes' George Russell by 0.009 seconds to take his first pole for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Title leader Kimi Antonelli, 20, qualified 5th but starts 4th after a grid penalty for Max Verstappen. Antonelli needs only a 9th-place finish or better to become F1's youngest-ever champion.
items.why_it_matters: A win or even a cautious points finish tonight could make Antonelli F1's youngest-ever world champion, beating Verstappen's old record.
items.context: Antonelli is a rookie who joined Mercedes this season after seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton moved to Ferrari. Mexico City's track sits over 2,200 metres up, where thin air changes how every car handles.
items.next: The race starts tonight, India time; a top-9 finish for Antonelli ends the title fight early.
items.insight: Needing only 9th means Mercedes can race for safety, not speed — expect Antonelli to avoid risk rather than chase the win.
